name: Buddy Sandboxes

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/gbmin (2026-11-08): "Both CPU-minutes and GB-minutes cost $0.00024." CPU-minute = vCPUs assigned x time; GB-minute = RAM assigned x time, so $0.0144 per vCPU-hour and $0.0144 per GB-hour of RAM, billed on allocation. "Sandbox & artifact storage" is $0.00011 per GB-hour (see storage). Pay-as-you-go needs Pro or Team: "The Free plan has no pay-as-you-go billing."

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Free includes Sandboxes and a $1/month usage credit (compute and storage), with no pay-as-you-go: "Once the credit is used up, pipelines and sandboxes stop" until next month (https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/gbmin, 2026-11-08). Free has "all the features of Buddy except SSO and advanced permissions" (https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/features). Marked trial_only because the engine has no hard usage cap: priced as unlimited usage at $0 fee it would be wrong. At the published rates $1 buys about 23 h of a 1 vCPU / 2 GB sandbox; a kept 50 GB disk alone costs about $4/month, more than the credit.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $29/month, 1 seat (extra $20/mo per seat), pay-as-you-go usage (https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/features, 2026-11-08). The pricing page shows the same fee as "€29 / month". The 2 "concurrents" are pipeline runners, not a sandbox cap (see fleet).

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $299/month, 1 seat (extra $30/mo per seat), pay-as-you-go usage, adds SSO (SAML, OIDC) and advanced permissions (https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/features, 2026-11-08). The pricing page shows "€299 / month".

caveats: Plans (rechecked 2026-11-08): Free $0 with a $1/month usage credit and no pay-as-you-go (sandboxes stop when the credit is spent), Pro $29/month and Team $299/month with pay-as-you-go usage. The docs list USD fees; the pricing page shows the same numbers in EUR. The old Hyper plan and the 300 sandbox CPU-minute allowance are no longer listed. Source: https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/features and https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/gbmin.

Rates (https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/gbmin, 2026-11-08): $0.00024 per CPU-minute and $0.00024 per GB-minute of RAM, both on allocation; sandbox storage $0.00011 per GB-hour, so disk_gib_month 0.0803 = $0.00011 x 730.
Sandbox concurrency limits per plan are not published.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

docker_inside=true per buddy.works/docs/sandboxes/introduction ("run Docker inside it"). Isolation "vm" is inferred from "behaves like a virtual machine you own" + kernel-parameter changes; the underlying hypervisor is not named. Nested virt / desktop not documented (null).

Coding agents: Buddy says "popular coding agents preinstalled" (https://buddy.works/docs/sandboxes/ai-agents). Driving agents by API: a documented Claude Managed Agents setup (Claude only) runs one worker sandbox per session from an orchestrator sandbox; workers get only a scoped ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY (https://buddy.works/docs/ai-agents/claude-managed-agents). Outside that setup no key proxy is documented, so other agents need their key inside the sandbox.
No sandbox timeout by default: a sandbox keeps running (and billing) until stopped unless a timeout is set; snapshots never expire and are not deleted with their sandbox.
Resources are fixed 2 GB per CPU presets from 1x2 to 12x24 (plus an undocumented 'CUSTOM' option in the API/YAML schema); disk is always 50 GB, not configurable.
Free workspaces are frozen after 60 days without a login and deleted 30 days later.

Free plan is not auto-picked (trial_only): it has no pay-as-you-go, so it covers only $1 of usage a month (about 23 h of a 1 vCPU / 2 GB sandbox). Workloads are priced on Pro ($29) or Team ($299) plus usage.

Stopped sandboxes keep billing for disk: "Compute stops being charged. The disk you keep is billed at the storage rate." (buddy.works/sandboxes FAQ, 2026-10-14). Disk is a fixed 50 GB, so at $0.00011 per GB-hour a kept sandbox costs ~$4/month in storage.

fleet.verification: Free signup explicitly says no credit card required.
fleet.notes: Pricing (2026-11-08) lists 2 concurrents on Free and Pro and 5 on Team ("extra: $5/mo. per concurrent"). Buddy's docs define these as pipeline runners: "Pipeline concurrency defines how many pipelines can run at the same time. When the number of triggered pipelines is greater that the number of runners in your plan, the subsequent executions get enqueued" (https://buddy.works/docs/pipelines/concurrency-and-parallelism, 2026-10-14). No sandbox concurrency cap is published; do not map pipeline slots to a VM quota.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The disk survives. Memory does not - running processes are terminated when the Sandbox stops, and apps are started again when it comes back up.
snapshot_auto.note: Stop (manual or inactivity timeout) keeps the 50 GB disk (persistent_disk), but no automatic snapshot/checkpoint is taken and memory is lost. Snapshots are taken by hand, from a pipeline action, or from inside via `this snapshot create`.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a saved state of a Sandbox at a point in time - the filesystem with everything installed and configured in it.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem only (no memory). UI/CLI/REST/SDK/MCP and from inside the sandbox (`this snapshot create`). 'Run in new sandbox' boots new machines from it ('One snapshot can back any number of Sandboxes'); 'Restore' reverts the source sandbox in place. Snapshots never expire and outlive their sandbox. Separate 'Clone' (copy of a sandbox) also exists.

harness_api.quote: Anthropic owns the agent loop, session state, event history, and the self-hosted work queue.
harness_api.how: deploy Buddy's Claude Managed Agents reference setup (github.com/buddy/claude-managed-agents): an orchestrator sandbox starts one worker sandbox per session; Claude only
harness_api.note: The Buddy SDK/API/CLI cover machine lifecycle, commands, files, apps and snapshots. The documented API-driven agent path is Claude Managed Agents: "the orchestrator picked up the session, spun up a fresh `cma-worker-<session>` sandbox from the snapshot." Other agents are started by your own code over a command.

ingress_rules.quote: Who is allowed through - an IP whitelist on any endpoint, plus Basic auth or Buddy auth on HTTP ones.
ingress_rules.note: Endpoints are tunnels via the in-sandbox bdy agent; nothing exposed unless you add an endpoint (SSH endpoint by default). Per-endpoint IP/CIDR whitelist, Basic auth, Buddy auth (signed-in Buddy users), user-agent whitelist, region choice.

guest_firewall.note: Docs: 'behaves like a virtual machine you own', passwordless sudo, 'change kernel parameters, run Docker inside it', each sandbox has its own network. Hypervisor not named; not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Variables are injected when the Sandbox starts, **before the first boot commands run**, so setup logic can rely on them.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are encrypted/masked variables injected as env vars, files or SSH keys inside the sandbox. No general credentials proxy is documented. Exceptions: git fetch/push to Buddy-connected repos is 'pre-authorized' and 'needs no tokens and no keys inside the Sandbox' (git only); and in the Claude Managed Agents setup "Your `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `BUDDY_TOKEN` stay on the orchestrator and never reach the execution layer", workers get only a scoped ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY (https://buddy.works/docs/ai-agents/claude-managed-agents, Claude only).

volume_attach.quote: This is why Sandboxes have no volumes or external drives to attach.
volume_attach.note: Fixed 50 GB persistent local disk. User can self-mount e.g. S3 buckets from inside (not first-party).

volume_shared.quote: This is why Sandboxes have no volumes or external drives to attach.
volume_shared.note: No first-party shared volume/FS; only DIY mounts (e.g. S3) from inside.

desktop.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine ... Terminal and SSH, Files, Running commands, Apps, Logs, Endpoints
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access is via browser terminal, SSH, or the SDK/CLI/API only; no VNC/RDP/graphical desktop stream is documented anywhere.

browser.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud. It has its own operating system, CPU and RAM allocation, a persistent disk, applications, and public endpoints
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Buddy Sandboxes are generic dev/CI Linux machines; no managed/pre-installed browser product is documented.

computer_use.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot+click driving API is documented; Sandboxes are driven via SSH/terminal/SDK/CLI/API, not a computer-use interface.

anti_bot.quote: 7-in-1 Pricing ... Sandboxes: password-protected public URLs & custom domains
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Buddy is a DevOps/CI-CD platform with generic sandbox machines; no stealth/fingerprinting/anti-bot feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: 7-in-1 Pricing ... Sandboxes: password-protected public URLs & custom domains
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented anywhere on Buddy's docs or pricing pages.

fork_running.quote: From inside the Sandbox - `this snapshot create -n before-migration` lets a script or an AI agent save a known-good state before a risky change.
fork_running.note: derived: snapshots (and by extension the Copy/Clone action, which also copies disk state) can be triggered from inside a live, running Sandbox via the self-management CLI, and the Clone API (POST /workspaces/:workspace/sandboxes with source_sandbox_id) documents no requirement that the source be stopped first.

pause_resume.quote: The Sandbox disk is persistent. Stopping or restarting a Sandbox does not erase anything ... A Sandbox can have a timeout - the number of seconds of inactivity after which it stops automatically.
pause_resume.note: Buddy's Stop/Start acts as pause/resume: compute stops accruing while STOPPED and the machine resumes on Start/auto wake-on-traffic. Stopped disk is still billed: buddy.works/sandboxes FAQ "What happens when a Sandbox stops? Compute stops being charged. The disk you keep is billed at the storage rate." The storage rate is $0.00011 per GB-hour ("Sandbox & artifact storage", https://buddy.works/docs/basics/billing-and-usage/gbmin).

own_agent_api.quote: A Sandbox is a clean, isolated machine with your repository already fetched, full sudo, and popular coding agents preinstalled.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Buddy offers an SDK/API/CLI/MCP to drive the SANDBOX MACHINE (create, clone, run commands, snapshot) and preinstalls third-party coding agents you SSH in and run yourself; there is no first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API.

public_ipv4.quote: Endpoints are tunnels: the Buddy agent (bdy) running in the Sandbox holds an encrypted connection to Buddy, and Buddy publishes it on an address it assigns. Nothing is exposed directly, and there are no ports to open.
public_ipv4.note: Access is via Buddy-assigned HTTP, TCP and TLS tunnel endpoints (EU, US or Asia) with IP allowlists, Basic or Buddy auth and custom domains. No public IP per sandbox is documented.

egress_allowlist.quote: How access to a Buddy Sandbox is calculated from project roles, direct assignments, and groups - plus repository and artifact access, tokens, and IP whitelists.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: only inbound controls are documented (per-endpoint IP whitelist, Basic/Buddy auth on tunnels, permission roles). No outbound/egress allow-list, deny-list, or no-internet mode is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: plus repository and artifact access, tokens, and IP whitelists
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rules are documented; only inbound tunnel/IP whitelisting exists.

static_egress_ip.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed/dedicated outbound IP product is documented anywhere in the sandbox docs or pricing page.

gpu.quote: Resources | From 1 CPU / 2 GB RAM up to 12 CPU / 24 GB RAM
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Resource presets are CPU/RAM only (1x2 to 12x24); no GPU option is listed anywhere in the sandbox docs or pricing page.

windows.quote: Operating system | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandboxes are Ubuntu Linux only; no Windows machine option exists.

macos.quote: Operating system | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandboxes are Ubuntu Linux only; no macOS machine option exists.

arm64.quote: Operating system | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
arm64.note: not offered: no CPU architecture choice is documented; the API's `resources` enum (1x2..12x24, CUSTOM) and OS list give no indication of an ARM image option.

self_host.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud.
self_host.note: not offered: Sandboxes run only in Buddy's managed cloud. Buddy separately advertises 'self-hosted runners and on-premises installation' for its CI/CD pipeline build agents, but that is a different feature from running the Sandboxes product on your own infrastructure, which is not offered.

byoc.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud.
byoc.note: not offered: no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment model is documented for Sandboxes; they run exclusively in Buddy's own cloud.

open_source.quote: buddy-works organization repositories: buddy-cli, buddy-works-node-api, buddy-works-php-api, passport-buddy, website ...
open_source.note: The Buddy platform (including Sandboxes) is closed-source SaaS; the GitHub org only publishes client SDKs/CLI wrappers, demo projects, and forks, not the core product under an OSI license.

hipaa.quote: PCI DSS CCPA GDPR ... SOC2 Type II certification
hipaa.note: not offered: the security page lists PCI DSS, CCPA, GDPR, and SOC2 Type II but never mentions HIPAA eligibility or a BAA offering.

eu_data_residency.quote: export BUDDY_REGION="US"   # optional, US by default, EU and AS available
eu_data_residency.note: Both the SDK/API workspace region and per-endpoint tunnel region (EU/US/AS) can be set to EU, allowing sandboxes and their traffic to be kept in the EU region.

max_session_h.quote: A Sandbox can have a timeout - the number of seconds of inactivity after which it stops automatically. There is no timeout by default.
max_session_h.note: A Sandbox keeps running (and billing) indefinitely until stopped, unless the owner sets an inactivity timeout themselves; there is no provider-imposed maximum session length.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The disk survives. Memory does not - running processes are terminated when the Sandbox stops, and apps are started again when it comes back up.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots and the 'Copy of an existing Sandbox' start point both only preserve filesystem/disk state ('a snapshot is a saved state of a Sandbox at a point in time - the filesystem with everything installed and configured in it', configuration.md: 'the copy includes the disk state'). No product surface captures or restores RAM/process state, so forking from a running memory state is not offered.

image_oci.quote: Whichever channel you use, a Sandbox starts from one of four sources: Clean OS ... Snapshot ... Copy of an existing Sandbox ... YAML definition
image_oci.note: The four documented starting points for a Sandbox are Clean Ubuntu OS, a Buddy snapshot, a copy of an existing Sandbox, or a YAML definition - none of them is a Docker/OCI image import. snapshots.md is explicit that Buddy's own snapshot mechanism substitutes for that workflow: 'Snapshots do the job of custom container images on other platforms. Instead of writing a Dockerfile, building it, and pushing it to a registry, you prepare a Sandbox once, save it, and start new machines from that state.'

egress_ip_type.quote: A Sandbox is an isolated Linux machine that runs in Buddy's cloud.
egress_ip_type.note: No dedicated/static or residential/mobile outbound IP product is documented anywhere (consistent with static_egress_ip:false); Sandboxes are generic multi-tenant cloud VMs, so outbound traffic uses ordinary shared cloud-datacenter IPs. Derived, not explicitly stated.

live_resize.quote: Grow the machine. Raise resources for a heavier build, then bring them back down. There is no dedicated flag for it - this update takes the full YAML definition: this yaml > /tmp/sandbox.yml # edit resources, e.g. to 4x8 ; this update @/tmp/sandbox.yml
live_resize.note: Resources (CPU x RAM, 1x2 to 12x24) can be changed on a live Sandbox from inside itself via `this update`, or externally via `bdy sandbox update` / PATCH /workspaces/:workspace/sandboxes/:sandbox_id (resources is an editable field), without recreating or wiping the machine.

usage_api.quote: Sandboxes: GET List Sandbox Snapshots, POST Create Sandboxes, GET Get Sandbox, PATCH Edit Sandbox, DEL Delete Sandboxes. Platform Account management: GET Get user, PATCH Update user, Emails, Personal Access Tokens, SSH keys, Projects, Permissions, Workspaces, Integrations, Variables. No billing, usa
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Billing information (GB-minutes usage) exists only via web dashboard. The REST API covers full sandbox lifecycle (create, start, stop, restart, clone, snapshot, run commands, upload files) but provides no programmatic access to billable usage per sandbox, per-tag, or per-project. Usage tracking is not available through REST API, SDK, or CLI.

locations_quote: export BUDDY_REGION="US"   # optional, US by default, EU and AS available
